title: How South Korea's Foreign Students Work — Survey
paragraphs: More and more students from other countries are studying in South Korea. Many of them also have part-time jobs. A new study shows what kind of work they do.

The study was done by the Migration Research and Training Center in South Korea. It found that 71.1% of foreign students who work have jobs in restaurants and hotels. For young students aged 19 to 24, the number was even higher, at 81.6%. Only a very small number of students had jobs connected to what they study.

Why do they choose these jobs? For 54.4% of students, the most important thing was working hours that fit with their classes. For 24.8%, pay was the most important thing. Only 2.4% said it was important that the job matched their studies or future career.

The study also found a problem. About 41.9% of students worked without officially reporting their jobs. Instead, they only had spoken agreements with their employers. One reason is health insurance. Students get a 50% discount on health insurance, but they lose it if they earn more than 3.6 million won a year.
Students said they also face other problems at work, such as language difficulties, unfair treatment and hard physical work.
The number of foreign students in South Korea is growing fast. In February 2026, there were about 314,400.
The researchers suggested that the government should create a better system to manage student part-time work and change the health insurance rules.
